thrifty

THRIF-tee · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Thrifty is very careful with money/resources.

The magazine's most popular column offered thrifty tips for feeding a family of five on a tight weekly budget.

Example

Instead of buying a brand-new car, the thrifty engineer bought a reliable used one and kept driving it for fifteen years, putting the savings toward his retirement.

Making sensible, deliberate choices to spend less, without going without what really matters, is exactly what thrifty describes.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

frugal: Frugal means sparing with money and resources, often shading toward plainness — a frugal supper is a simple one. Thrifty names the same care with a warmer face: it praises the cleverness of managing and stretching money well, not the bareness of doing without.

economical: Economical means giving good value for what is spent — an economical car sips fuel, an economical recipe stretches cheap ingredients — and it describes things as easily as people. Thrifty is more personal: it praises a person's steady, resourceful habit of making every dollar work.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

wasteful: using more than necessary, carelessly

extravagant: spending much more than necessary

Where it sits · how far the saving habit goes — careful → thrifty → austere

careful vs. thrifty: Careful is weaker than thrifty: a careful shopper just pays attention to prices, while a thrifty one goes further, making saving and stretching every dollar a steady habit.

austere vs. thrifty: Austere is more extreme than thrifty: a thrifty person economizes wisely, while an austere lifestyle goes further, stripping away comforts until only the bare essentials remain.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — thrive (þrífask)

root — thrive (þrífask): to prosper, to grow successfully (Old Norse)

Put it together

Put it together: Thrifty grew out of thrift, which originally just meant 'the condition of thriving.' Someone thrifty manages money so well that their household continues to thrive.

Use the root in a new word: thrive

Use the root in a new word: thrive: Even in the rocky, sandy soil, the old olive trees continued to thrive.

Strength Check

Word Choice

Thrifty is a warm, approving word for careful spending, a genuine virtue. Compare parsimonious (earlier in this unit), which describes the same careful habits pushed to an unpleasant, stingy extreme.
